belief: I have to keep everyone in my family happy.
origins: Some of us became the family peacekeeper early, learning to read moods and smooth things over before anyone exploded. We may have been rewarded for it or been afraid not to. As adults, we can feel responsible for everyone’s feelings at holidays, in group chats, and in every decision, and exhausted by the effort.
teaches: Proverbs says, “The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.” Paul says, “If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone,” which acknowledges that sometimes it is not possible. He also writes of seeking to please God and not people: “Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God?” and “each one should carry his own load.” Jesus Himself “frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray,” though people were still in need. Peacemaking is a calling. Keeping everyone happy is not.
self_statements: If someone is upset, I must have done something.
I cannot say no without causing a blowup.
I have to make sure everyone has a good time.
It is my job to keep the peace.
I cannot relax until everyone is okay.
errors: Treating other people’s feelings as my responsibility.
Trying to predict and manage everyone’s reactions.
Insisting that I should keep everyone satisfied.
Imagining that one unhappy person will ruin everything.
questions: When did I first become the one who kept everyone happy?
What do I fear will happen if someone is upset with me?
What are others responsible for in managing their own feelings?
What is the difference between peacemaking and people-pleasing?
What would I do differently if I trusted God with the outcome?
What is one small thing I can let others handle?
truth: I can be kind and a peacemaker without being responsible for everyone’s happiness. Each person carries their own load, and God is the one I ultimately answer to. I can set small limits and trust God with how others respond.
hw_truths: The fear of man is a snare.
I can live at peace as far as it depends on me.
Each person carries their own load.
I can trust God with others’ reactions.
log: Each week, write one task or feeling you let someone else carry.
actions: Write what you try to manage for others at gatherings.
Choose one thing to hand to someone else this week.
Rehearse a kind, short way to decline.
Withdraw to pray, like Jesus did.
prayer: Father, I have tried to keep everyone happy and I am worn out. Teach me to be a peacemaker without carrying what is not mine. Help me trust You with how others feel. Amen.
hw_questions: When did I become the peacekeeper?
What is one thing I can release?
How can I say no kindly?
When can I be alone with God?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Trusting the Lord sets me securely on high, even when someone is unhappy.”
